parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Complete the equation for this decay.

$${}^{211}_{84}\mathrm{Po} \rightarrow {}^{......}_{......}\mathrm{Pb} + {}^{......}_{......}\alpha$$

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Use Fig. 9.1 to determine the decay constant $\lambda$ of polonium-211. Give a unit with your answer.

$\lambda =$ .............................. unit ..................

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Use your answer in (b)(i) to calculate the activity at time $t = 0$ of the sample of polonium-211.

activity = .................................................... Bq

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: On Fig. 9.1, sketch a line to show the variation with $t$ of the number of lead nuclei in the sample.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Each decay releases an alpha particle with energy $6900\,\mathrm{keV}$.
parts.text:
Calculate, in J, the total amount of energy given to alpha particles that are emitted between time $t = 0.30\,\mathrm{s}$ and time $t = 0.90\,\mathrm{s}$.

energy = ....................................................... J

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest why the total amount of energy released by the decay process between time $t = 0.30\,\mathrm{s}$ and time $t = 0.90\,\mathrm{s}$ is greater than your answer in (c)(i).

stem: Polonium-211 (${}^{211}_{84}\mathrm{Po}$) decays by alpha emission to form a stable isotope of lead (Pb).
